entries.subject: An isolated working timber mitre lock gate mechanism with visible controlled water.
entries.brief: ONE PAIR OF HISTORICAL WOODEN MITRE LOCK GATES as a compact isolated FUNCTIONAL APPARATUS, shown in three-quarter view. The two broad timber gate leaves meet to form a shallow V pointing upstream; their edges connect properly, dark iron straps and hinges reinforce warm brown oak planks. Two balance beams extend from the gate tops toward their respective outer hinge posts, visibly attached. A SMALL bounded wedge of dull green-grey WATER sits just upstream behind the gates, with a lower visible water patch immediately downstream. ONE inset sluice paddle near the bottom is slightly raised and a small clear stream of water flows through its actual rectangular opening into the downstream water. The water belongs to the mechanism, not a scenic canal. Only minimal attached side hinge posts, no long masonry lock chamber, landscape, vegetation, sky, buildings, towpath, boat, human, scenic baseplate, frame or floor. This is a TECHNOLOGY object icon, never a building vignette. No detached beams, waterfall through solid timber, modern railings or neon blue water.

refs.title: How canal locks work — Canal & River Trust
refs.note: Gate and water-control principles; isolated apparatus is a simplified visual adaptation.

refs.title: Salterhebble Top Lock — Historic England
refs.note: Circa 1779 timber gates and balance beams; image search used as construction reference.

entries.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: one transparent painted TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3 / 1776 Age of Revolutions.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: five folded newspapers in a compact fan, currently containing two copies of Le Figaro.
Change ONLY the SMALL REAR-LEFT newspaper masthead that currently reads "LE FIGARO", behind National Intelligencer and to the left of the tall central Chinese newspaper. Replace this small duplicated masthead with "ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG", a genuine nineteenth-century German newspaper name, complete on TWO centered lines if needed:
ALLGEMEINE
ZEITUNG
Exact spelling: A L L G E M E I N E, then Z E I T U N G. Use clear dark period serif or readable German blackletter. Keep the title aligned with that paper's perspective and within its actual top margin.
DO NOT change the LARGE FOREMOST FRONT-RIGHT "LE FIGARO" masthead.
Preserve the other three mastheads exactly: "LE CONSTITUTIONNEL" at far left; "NATIONAL INTELLIGENCER" at front-left on two lines; "京報" on the tall central rear newspaper, exactly those two traditional characters.
There must remain exactly FIVE physical newspapers with FIVE distinct names. No other readable words, dates, numbers, prices, article headlines, slogans, watermarks or logos. Body copy remains small abstract charcoal printing texture and the Chinese paper retains abstract vertical ink columns.
Preserve the existing fan arrangement, coherent overlaps, paper edges, folds, curls, nearly-white ivory paper, fine matte grain, painted volume, neutral natural colors, restrained upper-left light and overall compact silhouette as closely as possible. The requested change is only the one duplicated masthead, not a redesign.
No press machine, props, background, blue tint, scenery, floor, cast ground shadow, frame or medallion. This is a painted technology icon, not a building vignette or a production-method glyph.
Output on a square high-resolution canvas, at least 1024 pixels, with generous empty margins, true transparent alpha around the full physical paper silhouette and through gaps, never a baked black/white/checkerboard background. All paper edges remain uncut.

entries.subject: Two clasped hands as a compact painted symbol of mutual aid.
entries.brief: ONE compact, plainly understandable HANDSHAKE: TWO human hands clasped firmly in mutual aid, shown as a coherent pair of hands and short wrists with simple nineteenth-century cloth cuffs. Anatomically correct grip, thumbs properly opposed over the grasp, five fingers per hand, no extra fingers, no fused or severed anatomy. One off-white linen cuff and one subdued brown woven cuff, both attached naturally to their wrists. Modest natural skin tones and restrained painted highlights, not gold embossed metal. Strong broad joined-hands silhouette; entire cuffs included and softly finished within the object silhouette, no edge cropping. This is a CONCEPTUAL TECHNOLOGY ICON, not a poster, seal or bronze badge. No coin, circular emblem, laurel wreath, stars, flags, hammer/sickle, slogan, modern suit sleeve, gold halo, blood, building, people or background. The handshake communicates cooperation and solidarity, not a precise portrait or exact national emblem. Human hands are the deliberate primary subject here, overriding the generic no-people/no-hands rule used for machines.

refs.title: Mutual aid banner, 1890–1899 — Italian Ministry of Culture
refs.note: Later nineteenth-century clasped-hands emblem as solidarity motif, not copied banner or proof of a unique early socialist insignia.

refs.title: Workers' symbolism — Museum Wales
refs.note: Clasped hands are among working-class symbols; conceptual adaptation rather than exact era-specific badge.
